cros_ec: Add I2C and LPC probe methods for CrOS EC This patch adds the I2C and LPC methods as fallbacks in cros_ec_setup() and updates platforms to use it. Since Daisy, Spring and Skate fallback to raw I2C they still need a custom setup function to hook up I2C address structs in the private data. Link, Slippy, and Rambi fallback to raw IO, but since the IO addresses for that are standard in generic CrOS EC LPC code we don't need to do anything special and can remove ec.c for those boards. BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=tested "mosys ec info" on veyron_mighty, paine (would be nice to test on daisy, spring, or snow as well...) Signed-off-by: David Hendricks <dhendrix@chromium.org> Change-Id: I2ea1171a93b5fcf761f742be2e95047b2bd12b2b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/431520 Commit-Ready: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org>

cros_ec: Clean-up internal and public interfaces When CrOS EC was first added the board code did a lot of the work and a lot of functionality had to be exposed. Now that we've standardized and consolidated things we can clean-up the "public" API used by board-level code and limit scope of most lowlevel functions. A new header, cros_ec_internal.h, is created to contain the "private" API for functions which are called among the drivers. And while we're at it, move cros_ec_lock.h since it should not be needed outside the CrOS EC drivers. This patch opportunistically removes cros_ec_hello() which isn't used. Also, since the probe functions set up the EC/PD interfaces we can rename them to imply setup (cros_ec_probe_* -> cros_ec_setup_*). BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=compiled for amd64 and arm-generic Change-Id: I6ba94f9cd1cecd2fd0403717afab804a8db56c7c Signed-off-by: David Hendricks <dhendrix@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/434317 Commit-Ready: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: clk: rockchip: Set "ignore unused" for PMU M0 clocks on rk3399 The PMU Cortex M0 on rk3399 is intended to be used for things like DDRFreq transitions, suspend/resume, and other things that are the purview of ARM Trusted Firmware and not the kernel. As such, the kernel shouldn't be messing with the clocks. Add CLK_IGNORE_UNUSED to these clocks. Without this change, the following was observed on a Chromebook with a rk3399 (using not-yet-upstream ARM Trusted Firmware code and not-yet-upstream kernel code based on kernel-4.4): 1. We init the clock framework. 2. We start up "DDRFreq", which causes ATF to occasionally fire up the M0 for transitions. Each time ATF fires up the M0 it will turn on these clocks and each time it is done it will turn them off. 3. We finally get to the the part of the kernel that calls clk_disable_unused() and we disables the clocks. You can see the race above. Basically everything is fine as long as ARM Trusted Firmware isn't starting up the M0 at exactly the same time that the kernel is disabling unused clocks. ...but if the race happens then we go boom.
